geometry_edits.rationale: Use the existing bend node as the dominant form controller, since the candidate is already coherent and only needs a stronger continuous gesture.
Reduce the curvature slightly to keep the mass calm and capacity-bearing rather than overly sculptural.
Preserve the longitudinal bending logic that supports a readable bar condition.
Upgrade the small notch into a true courtyard/public void so the ground plane and frontage can read as a usable neighborhood threshold.
Enlarge the void enough to register in plan and section as public space rather than a minor incision.
Orient the void to the site-access side so the street edge becomes legible and active.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the bar into a more legible curved dominant gesture that can better support a neighborhood street building and make the active edge read as intentional rather than generic.
Keep the bend aligned with the long axis so the dominant mass remains continuous and readable across views.
Slightly reduce the bend intensity to preserve a calm primary mass while keeping the gesture clear.
Convert the small cave into a more public and legible court/void so the ground threshold responds to the access edge and improves program fit.
Enlarge the void enough to read as usable public space rather than a decorative subtraction.
Align the opening to the programmed access side so the public threshold is clearly articulated toward the street.

rationale: The candidate reads as one dominant, coherent bent bar in all four views, so it clears the basic massing coherence gate. The silhouette is legible and not over-fragmented; the repair also appears geometrically intact. The main weakness is programmatic ground response: the mass does not strongly articulate the verified access edge with a public void, court, or seam, and the central void logic is only modestly expressed in the views. As a neighborhood-living mass, it is plausible, but it leans more toward an abstract sculpted bar than an explicitly active street building. The form resonates well with the curved bar/community-center references, but section/roof logic remains relatively generic rather than clearly supporting a more public threshold or inhabited terrace condition.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Curved continuous massing with a central void and bridge-like upper connection; good match for a compact neighborhood building with an explicit public opening.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More fragmented and campus-like than the candidate; do not copy the multi-wing complexity.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking low-rise volumes with a courtyard void and layered horizontal hierarchy; useful for preserving a dominant mass with public ground organization.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much flatter and more orthogonal than the candidate.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Simple low-rise pavilion with a clear entry canopy and restrained rectilinear massing; useful as a calm active-edge datum.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Counterfactual: large waterfront housing composition, not a neighborhood street-building precedent.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/courtyard section logic can inform public void and stepped inhabitation, but the scale and residential hybrid typology are too different to imitate directly.

warnings: Access edge response is under-articulated relative to the required active ground threshold.
Void/publicness is present only weakly; consider a clearer notch, court, or undercut aligned to the frontage.
The form is coherent, but the program reading is slightly generic for neighborhood living.
